To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystals of the complex diffract X rays to beyond 1 A and are suitable for structure solution by molecular replacement.
we have determined the structure of Scilla campau-lata agglutini in complex with the disaccha-ride mannose-α(1,6)d-mannose to 1.8 A resolution.
we have determined the structure of Scilla campamulata lectin (SCL) complexed with the α1,6 mannobioe disaccharide to 1.5 A resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of the lectin from Scilla campanula and the characterization of its structure.
the structural and functional characterization of Scilla campau-lata agglutini, a mannose-specific lectin from bluebells.
the isolation, purification and characterization of lectins, and with the structural and functional characterization of the carbohydrate-binding sites of these proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the crystals belong to space group P212121 with a dimer as the asymmetric unit and that the structure is being solved by molecular replacement using the known structure of Scilla cam-panulata ag- glutinin.
the crystal structure of the complex of Scilla cambanulata lectin and α1,6 mannobiose has been determined to a resolution of 2.0 A.
this work has provided a good starting point for the structure determination and characterization of the Scilla campanula lectin complexed to the disaccharides mannose and mannose-α(1,6)–mannose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully crystallized a lectin complexed to a specific carbohydrate.
Scilla campanyulata agglutinins (SCAs) have been crystallized and the crystals are stable in an intense synchrotron X-ray beam.
Scilla campamulata agglutin has been crystallized and the structure solved by the molecular-replacement technique.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of this lectin complexed to a disaccharide is very similar to that of the native lectin.
the structure of the ScaL complex with mannobiose is very similar to the structure of the lectin complexed to mannose.
Scilla campau-lata agglutinnin has a strong affinity to α(1,4)-linked mannosides and α(1-6)-linked disaccharides.
